title: Follow one DST step through the code
orientation:
**Run:** 1 Start → 2 Read paused calls → 3 Choose one action → 4A Write or 4B Control → 5 Check. A passing step returns to 2; after the configured steps, 6 checks the settled system.

**Example:** One step starts a client commit. After that step settles, the next step can see its paused call and start another write, advance it, or drop a server handoff. A mismatch can be reproduced at 7.

sections.heading: 1. Start: execute() boots the world, then enters the step loop
sections.output: two booted clients, a server, and the first call to world.pending()

notes.text: Creates the server, clients, Gatekeeper, and reference model before any step runs.
Every step first reads paused calls, then chooses one possible action.
The chosen action becomes a trace record; it need not finish a whole commit.
After applying the action, check state before starting the next step.

notes.anchor: for (const name of clientNames) await world.boot(name)
notes.text: Both clients connect before fault-controlled steps begin.
From this point, handoffs can stop and the loop can order them.

sections.heading: 2. Read: world.pending() gives choose() the calls stopped right now
sections.input: Gatekeeper calls held at their current boundary
sections.output: one snapshot of named, actionable paused calls

notes.text: The first snapshot may be empty. Later snapshots include commits that reached a gate.
Stable names let the trace refer to the same call during replay.

blocks.label: Gatekeeper reports only the current stop

notes.text: Each call contributes at most one current stop.
Finished or already controlled calls are not offered to the loop.
The stop says who sent the call and which service it waits for.

sections.heading: 3. Choose: the pending snapshot becomes one enabled action
sections.input: paused calls plus which clients can write, crash, or restart
sections.output: one set, remove, advance, drop, crash, or restart intent

blocks.label: Only server handoffs may be dropped

notes.text: The old test could also drop a local storage write.
The fault choice now considers only handoffs crossing the server boundary.

blocks.label: The chooser selects one possible event

notes.text: A drop is possible only when a droppable call exists and this seeded draw selects it.
A new write may start even while another call is paused.
Otherwise the loop can pick one held call to move forward.

blocks.label: What counts as a server handoff

notes.text: A request, reply, or poke touches the server. Local timer and disk calls do not.

sections.heading: 4A. If set/remove: apply() starts a commit and leaves it in flight
sections.input: a set or remove intent from choose()
sections.output: a local write plus a commit promise that can pause at a gate

notes.text: The chosen client opens a local transaction.
The independent model records the write before any server acknowledgement.
The commit starts without waiting for completion. Its next stop can appear in step 2 on a later iteration.

sections.heading: 4B. If advance/drop/crash/restart: apply() controls one existing action
sections.input: a named paused call or a running/down client
sections.output: one call moved or failed, or one client lifecycle change

notes.text: Advance releases this call toward its next boundary, where it may pause again.
Drop fails this particular handoff.
Crash stops one running client.
Restart creates a new client over the same durable storage.

sections.heading: 5. Check: settle launched work, compare state, then loop or stop
sections.input: effects of 4A or 4B, including any server response that arrived
sections.output: a violation, or another iteration beginning at step 2

blocks.label: Wait only for this step to settle

notes.text: Promise continuations reach a stable boundary; this does not finish every commit.
Then compare each running client with the reference model.

blocks.label: Compute what a client should show

notes.text: Begin with the last server state this client received.
Overlay this client’s own writes that are still unacknowledged.
Read the real client database, independently of the model.
A mismatch stops the run at this step; otherwise execute() starts the next iteration.

sections.heading: 6. Finish: drain all calls, then check clients and server together
sections.input: the last step’s state, or a violation already found during the loop
sections.output: final client/server states and a violation if either side disagrees with the model

blocks.label: Settle and reconnect before the final comparison

notes.text: Release the gates and finish every in-flight call before judging the final state.
Each client gets a final chance to receive the server’s state.
The final check includes the server, so two matching clients cannot hide a wrong server state.
Also flag writes that never reached the server.

blocks.label: Compare the real server with the model

notes.text: Read what the real server stored.
Compare it with mutations the model observed the server accept.

sections.heading: 7. If a failure is saved: replay feeds the same actions into a fresh world
sections.input: the recorded seed and event trace from an early or final violation
sections.output: the same violation, or the first point where replay diverges

notes.text: Replay uses the saved choice instead of drawing a new random one.
If that action is no longer possible, report divergence at this step.
Apply the same intent to a fresh world.
Run the same state check after the replayed action.
